t: This is the Royal Watercolour Society, a British institution of painters working in watercolour. It was founded in 1804, and William Frederick Wells is named as its founder, alongside other artists including Nicholas Pocock, Peter De Wint, Samuel Shelley, William Sawrey Gilpin and Cornelius Varley. Pocock was best known for marine art. Varley was also an inventor, who made the graphic telescope and the graphic microscope. Members use the letters RWS or ARWS after their names, and they are elected by the membership, with about half a dozen new associates joining each year.
